newsitem.title: UK: LPC-Turkcell mandates trio for $575 mln funding.
newsitem.headline: LPC-Turkcell mandates trio for $575 mln funding.

text.p: LONDON July 30 (LPC) - Turkcell, Turkey's leading GSM operator, has mandated Bankers Trust, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and JP Morgan to lead a groundbreaking $575 million project financing.
The transaction is a rare example of Turkish corporate activity in the international capital markets, and is also one of the largest deals to emerge from Turkey this year.

The deal has been fully underwritten and comprises a $75 million bridge facility, a $350 million three-year syndicated loan and a $225 million five-year high-yield bond issue, which will be lead managed by Bankers Trust, the company announced.
The bridge loan will be used to fund the purchase of infrastructure equipment, and will be funded by the arrangers in mid August.

The longer term facilities, which will be used to finance the conversion of the company's build-operate transfer agreement into Turkey's first operating license, will take out the bridge facility, and will not be made available if Turkcell's license bid fails.
The process has been subject to considerable bureaucratic delay due to lack of precedent and changing administrations, but a decision is expected by October.

The syndicated element of the facility is highly unusual in terms of size and tenor. Lender appetite for medium-term Turkish credits is almost non-existant - bank borrowers have found it nearly impossible to tap the market for longer than one year, and the Republic of Turkey has also found it difficult to raise medium-term money.
Turkcell's sucess in achieving three-year financing is a significant pointer to the company's strategic importance.
Turkcell has an 85% share of Turkey's GSM market and 900,000 subscribers, and is one of Europe's top five GSM operators, but its healthy business prospects are constrained by country risk.

"Sovereign risk is a critical issue for favourable terms and this has proved to be a significant cost for us" said Cuneyt Turktan, Turkcell's general manager."Our all-in cost will be in the region of 9-9.5%." he added. The rarity of corporate deals, caused largely by foreign banks' insistence on expensive additional local bank guarantees, has given the arrangers few pricing benchmarks to work with. Market speculation puts the spread at 300 bps over LIBOR.
